newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil could have 6 pct GDP growth with reforms.
newsitem.headline: Brazil could have 6 pct GDP growth with reforms.

text.p: Brazil could increase the pace of economic growth to about six percent a year once Congress passes key structural reforms, a senior Finance Ministry official said.
However, the signs are that those reforms will have to wait until after next year's elections, Pedro Parente, the ministry's executive secretary said.

"Unfortunately, there is no reason to revise our current predictions of about four percent (GDP) growth a year, but the country's potential is for about 50 percent more than that," Parente told reporters at a seminar on public finance.
"It is now clear we are not going to be able to enjoy stronger growth precisely because we have not managed to implement reforms quickly enough," he said.
The government's pension and civil service reforms were sent to Congress two years but have run up against fierce resistance.

Government lawmakers now acknowledge they have little chance of getting both bills through Congress as the October 1998 presidential, congressional and state governorship elections begin to dominate Brazilian politics.
Parente said whoever won the next elections would have to address the pension and civil service reforms immediately. "The longer they are left, the more traumatic they will be."

He also said the proposals included in the reforms "were a step in the right direction," but would have to be deepened if Brazil was to catch up with changes implemented by other countries in Latin America.
